owl.title: How to ride the Owl Bus (N-bus)
owl.intro: After the last train, the Owl Bus connects central Seoul the same way a regular city bus does. All you need is the stop number and the direction.

s1.title: Find the route and direction
s1.desc: Enter a departure and destination on the home page to get direct or one-transfer trips with the boarding stop number. Tapping a station on the route map also shows stop numbers by direction.

s2.title: Find the stop by its number
s2.desc: Stops with the same name sit on both sides of the road and each direction has its own number. Open the map link for the exact spot and wait on the side with the matching number.

s3.title: Check first and last buses
s3.desc: Depending on the route, the first bus leaves its terminal between 23:10 and 00:00 and the last between 03:10 and 04:10. Route pages and the home status line show whether a route is in service now.

s4.title: Tap your card and transfer
s4.desc: Tap your transit card both when boarding and when getting off. Between 21:00 and 07:00 a transfer counts within 60 minutes of tapping out, with discounts for up to 4 transfers.

about.title: About Seoul Autonomous
about.intro: An independent guide to getting around Seoul after 11 pm, built on official data shown with its reference dates. Owl Bus (N-bus) routes, stops and transfers come first; autonomous night and early-morning routes are the secondary track.

who.title: Who makes it
who.body1: Seoul Autonomous is run independently by Dapala Corp (다파라코프), a registered business in Seoul. It is not affiliated with the Seoul Metropolitan Government, any bus operator, or map services such as Kakao or Naver.
who.body2: Dapala Corp runs the site by checking and processing Seoul public data and official notices directly, and corrects errors reported by readers. The route map was drawn by the operator; stop and timetable figures are copied unchanged from official Seoul data. The hand-written parts are the route descriptions and the choice of hubs.

why.title: Why it exists
why.body1: After the last train, the goal is to let you decide where and what to board right now in Seoul, with the official evidence next to the answer.
why.body2: It is built for designated drivers, night-shift workers, late-night commuters and visitors moving around at night, down to the stop number and direction.
why.body3: This is not a real-time transit app. It does not imitate arrival times, and it separates what was checked from what was not.

how.title: How it is built
how.item1: Owl Bus stops, stop order, coordinates and stop numbers (ARS): the Seoul Open Data Plaza bus-route stop dataset ({stops} snapshot), used as is.
how.item2: Owl Bus timetable (first and last bus, headway, fleet, distance): only the factual figures from the Seoul Metropolitan Government notice revised {schedule}.
how.item3: Route map: a schematic drawn by the operator from the Seoul data. Station positions are area markers; use the map links for the exact stop.
how.item4: 16 transfer hubs: stop groups (same name, within 400 m) where three or more Owl Bus routes meet.
how.item5: Autonomous routes (Simya A21, early-morning A routes, robotaxi): Seoul-provided information shown in Kakao Map, checked manually, with the check date ({auto}).
how.item6: What it does not do: no real-time-looking wording, no guessed values, no map-app logos.
how.link: See sources, licenses and dates by field

updates.title: Updates and history
updates.body: The data snapshot and timetable revision dates appear in the footer of every page. Structural or data changes are logged as update posts.

report.body: If a stop number, direction or first/last bus time looks wrong, email us. The report links on route and hub pages put the route or hub name in the subject.

earlyMorning.title: Seoul early-morning autonomous buses (Saebyeok routes)
earlyMorning.description: Seoul's Saebyeok early-morning autonomous buses A160, A741, A148 and A504: service areas, start dates, stop counts, boarding rules and shared owl-bus stops.
earlyMorning.intro: Seoul's {count} Saebyeok early-morning autonomous bus routes. Each leaves its starting stop once, at {time}, and makes one round trip.
earlyMorning.introFallback: These autonomous bus routes operate in the early morning hours before 5:00 AM. Check Kakao Map for the latest schedule before riding.

facts.note: Service areas and start dates follow Seoul's route overview of 27 April 2026. Stop counts and owl-bus overlaps were counted from this site's stop data.

rules.title: Before you ride
rules.express: A741, A148 and A504 run express, stopping only at the main stops with the most first-bus riders. Check the stop list on the route page, or search the route number in a map app, to see whether your usual stop is served.
rules.seats: No standing: once every seat is taken the bus takes no more passengers. Check free seats on the stop's bus information display (BIT) or the LED seat indicator on the front of the bus.
rules.tag: Tap your transit card when boarding and alighting, as on regular city buses.
rules.time: {time} on this site is the departure time at the starting stop. The Seoul announcements checked give no passing times for each stop, so none are shown.
rules.note: Items 1–3 are the boarding rules Seoul gave in its launch notices for A741 (29 March 2026), A148 (15 April) and A504 (27 April). Fares and operating days follow what each route page shows.

owl.schedule: The last buses on the {owlCount} owl routes leave their starting stops between {lastMin} and {lastMax}; the {count} Saebyeok routes leave theirs at {time}. Seoul describes Saebyeok buses as departing 30 minutes before the regular first city buses.

lateNight.title: Seoul late-night autonomous bus and robotaxi
lateNight.description: Seoul's two late-night autonomous services after 22:00 — the Simya A21 bus and the Gangnam robotaxi: hours, departures, fares, how to call and how to choose.
lateNight.intro: This page covers two autonomous services in Seoul after 22:00: the {bus} bus on a fixed route, and the {taxi}, called within a set zone.
lateNight.introFallback: These autonomous services operate late at night after 10:00 PM. Check Kakao Map for the latest schedule before riding.

a21.title: Simya A21 — Dongdaemun Station to Hapjeong Station
a21.route: Simya A21 starts at Dongdaemun Station, runs through Jongno, Gwanghwamun, Seodaemun, Sinchon and the Hongik University area to Hapjeong Station, then returns. It has {stops} stops.
a21.departures: Worked out from the listed hours ({first}–{last}) and the {headway}-minute interval, it leaves the starting stop {n} times a night: {list}.
a21.weekday: It is listed as a weekday service.
a21.owlAll: All {stops} stops share their stop number with owl night buses ({owlN} owl routes). With only {n} departures a night, check the owl routes at the same stop as well.
a21.owlSome: {shared} of its {stops} stops share their stop number with owl night buses ({owlN} owl routes). Check the owl routes at the same stop as well.

taxi.title: Gangnam Robotaxi — called within a zone
taxi.area: The Gangnam Robotaxi has no fixed route or stops. Within the {area}, you set a pick-up point and destination and call it in the {app} app.
taxi.fare: The fare is a flat base fare by time band, KRW {min}–{max}, regardless of distance or duration; a payment card must be registered in the app beforehand.
taxi.fleet: Seoul expanded the fleet to 19 vehicles from 20 August 2026.

choose.title: How to choose
choose.a21: If your destination is on the Simya A21 line (Dongdaemun – Jongno – Gwanghwamun – Sinchon – Hapjeong), see whether one of its departures ({list}) fits, and check owl buses at the same stop.
choose.taxi: If both your start and destination are inside the Gangnam pilot zone, that is the robotaxi's service range on weekdays, {start}–{end}.
choose.owl: For other night trips, check the {owlCount} owl bus routes too: pick your start and end stops in the home route finder or on the route map.
choose.days: Both Simya A21 and the robotaxi are listed as weekday services.
